newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch ECT named top bidder for Trieste terminal.
newsitem.headline: Dutch ECT named top bidder for Trieste terminal.

text.p: Dutch-owned Europe Combined Terminals (ECT) said on Wednesday it had been named as preferred bidder for the container terminal at the Italian port of Trieste.

ECT executive board member Barend Bosselaar said ECT was advised on Wednesday it had been placed at the top of a list of three bidders for the terminal, which is being privatised by the city of Trieste.
"That means we can enter into negotiations with the port authorities to see if we can come to terms to take over the (terminal)," he told Reuters.
ECT is owned about 30 percent by each of Koninklijke Nedlloyd Groep NV, Internatio-Mueller NV and Koninklijke Pakhoed, with state-owned Dutch Railways holding the other 10 percent.

He said no financial terms had yet been discussed but ECT's bid had included details of how it believed the terminal could be operated, the potential market opportunities and what ECT could contribute to developing the facility.
Trieste's proximity to Austria, Hungary and the former Eastern European states and its deep water location made it attractive, he added.
"The terminal is well equipped. I don't think we will have to invest very substantial sums," Bosselaar said.
